name: Immersion cooling
applications: Very high density racks where cold plates are insufficient
Edge and HPC deployments with constrained air handling
principle: Immersion cooling puts the server, or a sealed chassis, into a dielectric bath, so heat leaves by direct contact with liquid instead of air. Single-phase systems circulate the fluid to an external heat exchanger; two-phase systems let the fluid boil and condense on a coil. Because the whole board is wetted, density is limited by the tank and fluid rather than by a cold plate's coverage, but service procedures and fluid compatibility change completely.

process_steps.name: Servers are immersed in dielectric fluid
Fluid absorbs heat by conduction and convection
Heat is rejected to a facility water loop or dry cooler
Servers are drained and lifted for maintenance

performance.metric: liquid-cooled infrastructure deployed by one vendor
performance.basis: Submer home page: 500 MW+ liquid-cooled infrastructure deployed and 8 GW+ deployment-ready capacity, with 3 global R&D labs. Vendor-reported aggregate; no per-tank capacity given.

source.note: Submer Group home page (deployed capacity claims), read 2026-11-14

advantages: Removes the air-side limit on rack density
No fans in the tank, so IT fan power falls
Heat is available at a higher grade for reuse
limitations: Service and warranty implications for every server model
Fluid cost, handling and top-up are new operational disciplines
Very little independent operating data is public
